thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert -> inferpool-usw1: 5x NotReady events in 2m. Pager -> @maria (oncall). Incident INC-2026-0487 created. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC-2026-0487

maria (oncall): Acknowledged, I'm on it. Starting triage — checking node health and kubelet logs.

jon: On my way. Any customer impact yet?

maria (oncall): Quick check: node kubelet restarted multiple times. Running `kubectl get nodes` now.

maria (oncall): ```bash
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady
node-az3-57   NotReady   18m   kubelet_restart_count=3   10.2.33.57
```

maria (oncall): journalctl snippets look like driver/kernel OOM and runtime failures:
```text
Feb 17 12:34:56 node-az3-57 kubelet[1234]: E0217 12:34:56 kubelet.go:... runtime service error: container start failed: OOMKilled
Feb 17 12:34:57 node-az3-57 nvidia-containerd: error: failed to initialize cuda: driver reset in progress
```

sana: Are inference pods being evicted or stuck Pending on that node pool? That's customer-facing.

maria (oncall): `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep node-az3-57` shows a mix: several `Evicted` and a few `CrashLoopBackOff` for model-server containers. Not mass draining happening yet.

kevin: Let's avoid draining the whole node pool — draining will cause a surge of reschedules and might spike OOMs elsewhere. Suggested immediate action: cordon the flappy node(s) and steer new inference traffic away from the pool via routing policy.

maria (oncall): Cordoning node-az3-57 now (no drain): `kubectl cordon node-az3-57` -> node is Unschedulable.

maria (oncall): Applying routing patch to divert new requests from `gpu-infer-usw1` to `gpu-infer-use1` via smart routing.

deploy-bot: Routing policy update applied: policy-id=rp-42 change-id=ch-98765 (automation user)

jon: Good. Eng-runtime: logs mention `driver reset` and kernel OOM. Any recent driver or kernel changes on that pool?

eng-runtime: @maria @jon I'm oncall for runtime. We saw a newer NVIDIA driver (535.79.12) rolled to that pool last night in the image bake. Repro possible: kernel OOM on cuda processes under high batch. We'll spin a repro in staging with same driver/kernel and run a stress test. Short-term mitigation: lower default batch sizes and disable prefetch on that pool to reduce GPU memory pressure.

maria (oncall): Patching inference config to reduce batch_size -> 4 and disable prefetch for routes hitting gpu-infer-usw1. Patch applied.

sana: Customer impact: CS flagged 3 enterprise customers (ak-123, ak-987, ak-401) saw elevated 5xx rates (~6% over baseline) for ~5 minutes. No data loss reported. Status page draft ready.

kevin: Creating incident bridge in 5m. We'll keep this channel for coordination. If the node keeps flapping we'll replace the node rather than drain to avoid churn.

maria (oncall): Starting node-replace job for node-az3-57 (safe-replace, will create new node and cordon old). Kicking off now.

jon: Also capturing `dmesg` tail — kernel OOM lines:
```
[ 1234.567890] oom_reaper: reaped process 4567 (model-server), now anon-rss:0kB
[ 1234.567895] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

eng-runtime: That Xid 79 is a GPU reset. We should attempt a driver rollback on the node image after we stabilize. For now keep nodes cordoned and let autoscaler provision replacements with the previous image. I'll open an infra issue for a hotfix.https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/1234

sana: I'll update the status page: "Mitigation in progress, traffic rerouted, estimated recovery 60m" and notify affected customers.

maria (oncall): Node replacement started, new node registering as `node-az3-72` joining pool. Monitoring pods reschedule.

jon: Monitoring metrics: p95 latency on inference for region shows small uptick but backends are handling after routing change. No broad customer outage expected.

kevin: Post-incident action items: (1) revert driver roll in baked image, (2) add driver Xid monitoring to alert earlier, (3) add runbook step to cordon+replace vs drain for GPU nodes. Adding to INC ticket.

incident-bot: INC-2026-0487 status updated -> mitigating. Bridge: 10.0.0.5:5000. Owner: maria.

sana: I'll own comms and postmortem doc. Thanks all, keep channel updates short.

maria (oncall): Will keep monitoring; tagging eng-runtime for driver rollback plan. Leaving channel for pager rotations in 15m.

eng-runtime: Rolling follow-up: will prepare image with driver 530.x and coordinate with infra to roll to affected pools in maintenance window.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0487 -> last activity recorded. If new NotReady events occur, PagerDuty escalation will resume.
